questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: A mix of new academic opportunities and exploring new cultures.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was interested in Irish film and Irish history.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UCC is pretty good at giving information regarding arrival and uni.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: UCC hosted information seminars during freshers week (mandatory) which helped a lot. You can also go to their International Office and ask for help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was a little unorganized. I would have liked to know more about their system such as library system, but overall good.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Housing is really expensive, be prepared for that. I lived in dorms at YUGO Bottleworks whose daily management is not very efficient. I made really good friends here so I recommend it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Campus is a bit away from the city centre and there are no bigger supermarkets around. Took 15-20 mins by foot from my dorm to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You can enter a draw and get offered a place to live (usually dorms or shared housing). The standards of most the dorms are not good. You also have to buy your own cutlery, pots, pans, etc.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They forgot to send me the application form to me in the spring, so I almost didn't make it. Other than that, they have good guides to help you through their websites.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was done online. You must provide personal details.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They send you a guide along with the registration websites. You can also email International Office if you need help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful. During the first 1-2 weeks they have a trial period in which you can try out different kinds of subjects, so you can drop them if you don't want to take them anyway.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try out subjects that are not necessarily directly related to your degree. UCC offers Intro to Irish culture/language/history/and more!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had three BA courses and one MA course. The level of academia was pretty much the same as in Copenhagen, sometimes lower. I had a few written essays I had to hand it, and they were very short/small compared to the kind of essays I'm used to writing at home. I also did 3 creative video essays which was very challenging as I have never done that before.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's pretty much the same style of teaching as UCPH. Seminar/lectures with interaction between students and teacher - asking questions and such. Some TAs also taught. The teachers know their students very well. I didn't experience any group projects. We didn't do group discussions in class either which I'm very used to at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: FX2007 Contemporary Screen and Media /// FX2011 Contemporary Cinema /// FX3019 Gender and Contemporary Cinema /// FX6010 Irish Cinema, Contexts and Aesthetics.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really liked Irish Cinema - nice teachers and the assignments were at an appropriate level. It's an MA course.
Gender and Contemporary Cinema was also interesting but the workload was almost too much compared to my other courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Cost of living is less expensive than in Copenhagen. Housing is very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can join both clubs (sports) and societies. UCC also organizes trips around Ireland and I went on 2 of those.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the trips and parties organized by UCC. Join a club or a society.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Other cities in the country. Train and bus tickets are very cheap! I went to Galway, Limerick, and Dublin, as well as smaller villages in Cork County.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mainly just the dialect which was difficult at first. Other than that, people are very nice and helpful.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very social and want to talk.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get out and do something during the first weeks as people are quick to find friends. Go on trips to other parts of Ireland. Don't stress too much about uni.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk to people if you're in doubt about something.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making really good friends that I hope to keep in contact with after I return home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting over the initial homesickness I experienced in the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
